domain.name: LangChain Agent Development
domain.scope: Use current LangChain Python APIs to build and understand common agent patterns centered on create_agent, tools, state/memory, middleware, and retrieval.
domain.target_user: Python developer who is new to current LangChain agent development.
non_goals: LangSmith deployment and evaluation as a primary topic

mental_model.summary: A LangChain agent is a model running inside a configurable harness. The model receives messages, may choose tools, receives tool results, and continues until it can finish. The harness supplies prompt, tools, middleware, and state-related behavior; retrieval can be added as a tool or as a preceding retrieval pipeline.

goals.title: Build a basic LangChain agent
goals.outcome: A working create_agent instance accepts messages and returns a model response.
goals.why_it_matters: It establishes the minimal agent harness and invocation model.

goals.title: Build a tool-calling agent
goals.outcome: The agent can select and call a Python tool during its model loop.
goals.why_it_matters: Tool use is the core mechanism for extending an agent beyond model-only responses.

goals.title: Build a stateful conversational agent
goals.outcome: The agent preserves conversation state across turns using LangChain/LangGraph persistence mechanisms.
goals.why_it_matters: State turns isolated invocations into a continuing interaction.

goals.title: Build an agentic RAG agent
goals.outcome: The agent can decide when to fetch external knowledge and use the retrieved content when answering.
goals.why_it_matters: It combines agent decision-making with runtime knowledge retrieval.

goals.title: Add execution control with middleware
goals.outcome: The agent applies at least one middleware capability such as retries, guardrails, prompt transformation, summarization, or human approval.
goals.why_it_matters: Middleware is the main extension point for shaping harness behavior around the core loop.

main_processes.title: Build a basic LangChain agent
main_processes.outcome: A minimal agent returns a response to a user message.

main_processes.title: Build a tool-calling agent
main_processes.outcome: The agent calls an external tool when the request requires it and returns a final answer.

main_processes.title: Build a stateful conversational agent
main_processes.outcome: Conversation state persists across multiple turns in the same thread.

main_processes.title: Build an agentic RAG agent
main_processes.outcome: The agent can fetch relevant external knowledge at runtime and use it in its answer.

main_processes.title: Add middleware control to an agent
main_processes.outcome: The agent's execution is modified by a configured middleware behavior.

stages.title: Install LangChain
stages.local_goal: Make the LangChain runtime available.
stages.why_it_exists: The application needs the LangChain package and provider integration.
stages.local_outcome: LangChain can be imported and used.

implementation_details.title: Install LangChain and a provider integration
implementation_details.action: Create a virtual environment and install LangChain plus one model provider.
implementation_details.command: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -U langchain langchain-openai
implementation_details.expected_result: pip ends with 'Successfully installed'. `python -c "import langchain; print(langchain.__version__)"` prints a version and exits 0.
implementation_details.caution: Install into the virtual environment, never the system interpreter. A global install is the usual cause of 'module not found' in a project that looks right.

implementation_details.title: Set the API key the provider will read
implementation_details.action: Export the key in the shell that will run the code, or put it in a .env file.
implementation_details.command: export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...   # or: echo 'OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...' > .env
implementation_details.expected_result: echo $OPENAI_API_KEY prints a non-empty value.
implementation_details.caution: A key in .env is only read if something loads it. `python -c "import os; print(bool(os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')))"` prints True, or you have not finished this step.

implementation_details.title: Point the SDK at your provider, if it is not OpenAI
implementation_details.action: Skip this step if you use api.openai.com. Any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint has to be named explicitly, or the SDK sends your key to OpenAI by default.
implementation_details.command: export OPENAI_API_BASE=https://your-provider.example/v1
implementation_details.expected_result: `python -c "from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; print(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini').openai_api_base)"` prints the endpoint. It prints `None` if the variable is misspelled.
implementation_details.caution: The two are independent: without the base URL a valid key still fails, and the error names OpenAI's key page. Do not test this against `/models` -- plenty of compatible gateways serve that path without checking the key at all, so it answers 200 either way. Verify with one real call instead: `python -c "from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; print(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini').invoke('reply with the word ok').content)"`. Note the variable is `OPENAI_API_BASE`, not `OPENAI_BASE_URL` -- the latter is silently ignored and the only symptom is the 401 below.

implementation_details.title: Read the heredoc used to write files
implementation_details.action: Later Stages create files with `cat > tools.py <<'PY' ... PY`. The first line opens a heredoc: `cat` writes everything up to the line that says `PY`.
implementation_details.command:
cat > heredoc-demo.txt <<'TXT'
line one $HOME is not expanded
TXT
implementation_details.expected_result: `cat heredoc-demo.txt` prints `line one $HOME is not expanded`. The single quotes around the tag are what stop the shell from expanding `$HOME`.
implementation_details.caution: The closing `PY` must be flush left, on its own line, or the shell keeps waiting for input. This is the only place heredoc is explained, so a Stage that uses it assumes you have read this -- and the file it writes has to be one a later Stage actually reads.

example.summary: A fresh virtual environment with LangChain importable.
example.input: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -U langchain
example.note: The version line is the check: no version means the install did not land here.

stages.title: Configure a model
stages.local_goal: Provide a model that create_agent can use.
stages.why_it_exists: The agent loop requires a model to interpret messages and choose responses/actions.
stages.local_outcome: A usable model identifier or model instance.

implementation_details.title: Create a chat model and call it directly
implementation_details.action: Construct a model with no agent involved. If the model works here, every later failure is about the agent rather than about credentials.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; print(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini').invoke('reply with the word ok').content)"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `ok`.
implementation_details.caution: A 401 here means the key, the endpoint, or the model name is wrong -- check all three, in that order, because the three produce the same error. On a third-party endpoint the message also names platform.openai.com, which is misleading rather than evidence: the SDK does not know whose server it reached. A 429 means rate limited. Both look identical later inside an agent, which is why this step exists.

implementation_details.title: Every later command reads these from the environment
implementation_details.action: Notice that `ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini')` names no key and no endpoint. It picks both up from the variables the Foundation exported, which is why no later Stage repeats them.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; m = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'); print('key set:', bool(m.openai_api_key)); print('endpoint:', m.openai_api_base)"
implementation_details.expected_result: `key set: True`. The endpoint line prints your provider, or `None` on api.openai.com -- both are correct, and `None` here is not the bug that a `None` endpoint causes later.
implementation_details.caution: Changing the key or endpoint means re-exporting in every shell you run from; a terminal opened before the export still holds the old value. This is also why the model is the only per-command argument: the rest is environment, so all 15 later commands are identical in this respect.

example.summary: The model answers without any agent involved.
example.note: Isolating the model first means a later failure is never a key problem.

stages.title: Create the agent
stages.local_goal: Assemble the minimal agent harness.
stages.why_it_exists: create_agent is the primary constructor for a configurable LangChain agent harness.

implementation_details.title: Create the agent with no tools
implementation_details.action: Call create_agent with the model and a system prompt. Tools may be empty.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[], system_prompt='You answer in one short sentence.'); print('created')"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `created`.
implementation_details.caution: The first positional argument is the model. Passing a string there is the most common error, and it fails with a type error rather than a useful message.

example.summary: An agent object exists with an empty tool set.
example.note: No network call happens here, so this is safe to run offline.

stages.title: Invoke the agent
stages.local_goal: Send a user message through the agent.
stages.why_it_exists: Invocation executes the harness and model loop.

implementation_details.title: Invoke the agent with one user message
implementation_details.action: Pass a message dict with a human role and read the returned state.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Name one benefit of agents.'}]}); print(r['messages'][-1].content)"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints a sentence about the benefit of agents.
implementation_details.caution: `r['messages'][-1]` is the final answer, not the first. With tools the first message is the model's tool request, so reading index 0 looks like a bug in the agent.

example.summary: A one-turn exchange returns a final message.
example.output: Agents can choose which tool to call for a given request.
example.note: messages[-1] is the answer; messages[0] is what you sent.

stages.title: Inspect the response
stages.local_goal: Read the final message returned by the execution.
stages.why_it_exists: The learner needs to connect runtime output back to the message-based mental model.

implementation_details.title: Read the whole message list
implementation_details.action: Print every message with its type so the execution is legible.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'}]}); [print(m.type, repr(m.content)[:60]) for m in r['messages']]"
implementation_details.expected_result: Two lines: `human 'hi'` then `ai ...`.
implementation_details.caution: The state is a dict with a 'messages' key. Reaching for `.content` on the result object instead is the usual cause of an AttributeError.

example.summary: The execution is two messages: the one sent and the one returned.
example.output: human 'hi' / ai 'Hello! How can I help you today?'
example.note: Reading types rather than text is what makes the tool loop legible later.

stages.title: Define a tool
stages.local_goal: Create an external capability available to the agent.
stages.why_it_exists: Tools give the model callable capabilities beyond text generation.
stages.local_outcome: A callable tool with an understandable input contract.

implementation_details.title: Write the tool as a typed function
implementation_details.action: Write a plain Python function with type hints and a docstring. The docstring is what the model reads to decide whether to call it.
implementation_details.expected_result: `ls tools.py` lists the file, and `python -c "from tools import word_count; print(word_count.invoke('a b c'))"` prints 3. The import is the real check: it fails if the heredoc never closed.
implementation_details.caution: A tool with no docstring still works but is called far less often: the model has nothing to match the user's request against.

example.summary: A typed function becomes a callable tool.
example.note: The docstring is the tool's description; without one it is rarely chosen.

stages.title: Create agent with tools
stages.local_goal: Attach the tool set while constructing the agent.
stages.why_it_exists: The harness must expose tools to the model loop.

implementation_details.title: Attach the tool at construction time
implementation_details.action: This imports tools.py, written by the step 'Define a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Pass the tool objects as the second argument to create_agent.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from tools import word_count; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[word_count]); print(list(a.get_graph().nodes['tools'].data.tools_by_name))"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `['word_count']`.
implementation_details.caution: Tools are bound at construction. Adding one to the list afterwards does nothing; the agent has to be created again.

example.summary: The constructed agent reports the tools it holds.
example.note: Tools bind at construction, so a later mutation has no effect.

stages.title: Invoke with a tool-requiring request
stages.local_goal: Run a request that requires external capability.
stages.why_it_exists: A suitable request makes the tool loop observable.
stages.local_outcome: An execution that may contain a tool call.

implementation_details.title: Ask something only the tool can answer
implementation_details.action: This imports tools.py, written by the step 'Define a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Invoke with a request that needs the external capability.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from tools import word_count; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[word_count]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'How many words are in: the quick brown fox jumps'}]}); [print(m.type) for m in r['messages']]"
implementation_details.expected_result: Four lines: human, ai (tool call), tool, ai (final answer).
implementation_details.caution: If you see only human and ai, the model chose not to call the tool. That is a prompt problem, not a wiring problem -- reword the request or the tool docstring.

example.summary: A tool-requiring request produces four messages.
example.input: 'How many words are in: the quick brown fox jumps'
example.output: human / ai(tool call) / tool(3) / ai(final answer)
example.note: Only human and ai means the model declined to call the tool.

stages.title: Verify the tool loop
stages.local_goal: Confirm that tool selection, tool execution, tool result, and final response occurred.
stages.why_it_exists: Tool calling is a loop, not merely a function existing beside the model.

implementation_details.title: Assert the four messages are present
implementation_details.action: This imports tools.py, written by the step 'Define a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Check the message types rather than reading the text.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from tools import word_count; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[word_count]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'count the words in: a b c'}]}); types = [m.type for m in r['messages']]; print(types); assert 'tool' in types, 'the tool never ran'"
implementation_details.expected_result: The list contains a `tool` entry and the assertion passes.
implementation_details.caution: Assert on types, not on wording. Checking for a specific number in the answer makes the test fail whenever the model phrases the result differently.

example.summary: The tool loop is confirmed by message types, not by wording.
example.input: assert 'tool' in [m.type for m in result['messages']]
example.note: Asserting on wording tests the model's phrasing, which is not the point.

stages.title: Configure persistence
stages.local_goal: Choose and configure the state persistence/checkpoint mechanism.
stages.why_it_exists: State must be stored between invocations if a conversation is to continue.
stages.local_outcome: A persistence mechanism available to the agent.

implementation_details.title: Choose a checkpointer
implementation_details.action: Use InMemorySaver while developing and SqliteSaver when the conversation has to survive a process restart.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver; print(type(InMemorySaver()).__name__)"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `InMemorySaver`.
implementation_details.caution: InMemorySaver loses everything when the process exits. A multi-turn demo that works until you restart is this mistake, not a LangChain bug.

example.summary: A checkpointer is constructed and usable.
example.note: In-memory state does not survive a process restart; use SqliteSaver for that.

stages.title: Create agent with persistence
stages.local_goal: Construct the agent with its persistence configuration.
stages.why_it_exists: Persistence behavior must be part of the running harness/graph.

implementation_details.title: Create the agent with a checkpointer
implementation_details.action: Pass the checkpointer into create_agent alongside the model and tools.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[], checkpointer=InMemorySaver()); print('created')"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `created`.
implementation_details.caution: An agent with a checkpointer but no thread_id raises at invoke time, not at creation time. The error appears one Stage later than the mistake.

example.summary: An agent holding a checkpointer is created.
example.note: A missing thread_id fails at invoke, one Stage after the mistake.

stages.title: Invoke within a thread
stages.local_goal: Execute multiple turns under the same conversation/thread identity.
stages.why_it_exists: State is useful only when later turns can recover the earlier thread state.

implementation_details.title: Invoke twice with the same thread_id
implementation_details.action: Send two turns in separate invoke calls, sharing one config.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[], checkpointer=InMemorySaver()); cfg = {'configurable': {'thread_id': 'demo-1'}}; a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'My name is Sam.'}]}, cfg); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is my name?'}]}, cfg); print([m.content for m in r['messages'] if m.type == 'ai'][-1])"
implementation_details.expected_result: The printed answer mentions `Sam`.
implementation_details.caution: The returned list ends with the question you just sent, so read the answer from the last `ai` message rather than `messages[-1]`. A new thread_id per call gives a new conversation every time, which looks like memory not working.

example.summary: Two turns under one thread_id form a conversation.
example.input: 'My name is Sam.' then 'What is my name?'
example.note: The same config object must be passed to both calls.

stages.title: Verify remembered context
stages.local_goal: Check that later turns use earlier conversational context.
stages.why_it_exists: This verifies actual continuity instead of merely configured persistence.

implementation_details.title: Assert the second turn saw the first
implementation_details.action: Ask for the name and check the answer mentions it. Asking for a name is the weak choice available here, so also print the message count, which is what actually distinguishes remembered from forgotten.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[], checkpointer=InMemorySaver()); cfg = {'configurable': {'thread_id': 'demo-1'}}; a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'My name is Sam.'}]}, cfg); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is my name?'}]}, cfg); print('kept', len(r['messages']), 'messages:', [m.type for m in r['messages']]); assert len(r['messages']) >= 3, 'the first turn was not carried over'; answer = [m for m in r['messages'] if m.type == 'ai'][-1]; assert 'Sam' in answer.content, 'the answer did not use the first turn'; print('remembered')"
implementation_details.expected_result: `kept 3 messages: ['human', 'ai', 'human']` and then `remembered`. Three messages on the second call means the first turn came back with the history; an agent with no checkpointer returns two.
implementation_details.caution: Read the answer out of the last `ai` message, not `messages[-1]`. With a checkpointer the list ends with the question you just asked, so `[-1]` is that question and asserting on it can never succeed. If only two messages come back, the model answered from general behaviour rather than from your thread. If this fails outright, check the thread_id first and the checkpointer second: a recreated agent with a fresh checkpointer starts empty every run.

example.summary: The second turn demonstrably used the first.
example.note: The message count is the test; the name alone can be guessed.

stages.title: Prepare knowledge access
stages.local_goal: Make external knowledge queryable at runtime.
stages.why_it_exists: RAG addresses finite context and static model knowledge by retrieving relevant external information.
stages.local_outcome: A searchable or directly queryable knowledge source.

implementation_details.title: Create the document the retriever will read
implementation_details.action: Write the source text to a file first. The next step loads this path, so it has to exist before anything can retrieve from it.
implementation_details.command:
cat > notes.txt <<'TXT'
The retry limit is three attempts.
Uploads above 20 MB are rejected by the API.
Session state is kept per thread_id, not per user.
TXT
implementation_details.expected_result: `cat notes.txt` prints the three lines above.
implementation_details.caution: A retriever over a file you did not write cannot be verified: the answer is then indistinguishable from the model answering from memory, which is the exact failure this Goal exists to rule out.

implementation_details.title: Load and split a document set
implementation_details.action: Load the text, split it into overlapping chunks, and keep the chunks in memory.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain_community.document_loaders import TextLoader; from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter; docs = TextLoader('notes.txt').load(); chunks = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50).split_documents(docs); print(len(chunks))"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints a chunk count greater than zero. Two extra packages are needed for this step alone: `pip install -U langchain-community langchain-text-splitters`.
implementation_details.caution: A zero here usually means the file path is wrong, not that the splitter is broken. Check the path before changing the chunk size.

example.summary: A document set is split into retrievable chunks.
example.note: Zero chunks means the path is wrong, not that the splitter failed.

stages.title: Expose retrieval as a tool
stages.local_goal: Give the agent a callable route to external knowledge.
stages.why_it_exists: In agentic RAG, retrieval can be provided as one or more tools that the agent chooses when needed.
stages.local_outcome: A retrieval tool accessible to the agent.

implementation_details.title: Wrap the retriever as a tool
implementation_details.action: Write a function that searches the documents and returns text.
implementation_details.command:
cat > search.py <<'PY'
from langchain.tools import tool

CHUNKS: list[str] = []

@tool
def search_notes(query: str) -> str:
    \"\"\"Search the project notes and return matching text.\"\"\"
    hits = [c for c in CHUNKS if query.lower() in c.lower()]
    return "\n".join(hits[:3]) or "no match"
PY
implementation_details.expected_result: `python -c "import search"` exits 0. An import failure here is almost always an unclosed heredoc rather than bad Python.
implementation_details.caution: Returning an empty string makes the model believe the answer is 'nothing found'. Return an explicit 'no match' so it can say so.

example.summary: The retriever is callable from the agent.
example.output: The retry limit is three attempts.
example.note: Return an explicit 'no match' rather than an empty string.

stages.title: Create retrieval-enabled agent
stages.local_goal: Construct the agent with retrieval capability and useful instructions.
stages.why_it_exists: The model needs both the retrieval capability and context about when to use it.
stages.local_outcome: An agent capable of deciding when to retrieve.

implementation_details.title: Create the agent with the retrieval tool
implementation_details.action: This imports search.py, written by the step 'Wrap the retriever as a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Pass the search tool and a system prompt that permits using it.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from search import search_notes; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[search_notes], system_prompt='Use search_notes for anything about the project notes.'); print('created')"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `created`.
implementation_details.caution: Without a system prompt the model often answers from its own knowledge instead of retrieving, and the agent looks broken when it is merely misdirected.

example.summary: The agent is told it may retrieve.
example.note: Without the system prompt the model often answers from memory instead.

stages.title: Run a knowledge-dependent request
stages.local_goal: Ask a question that requires external knowledge.
stages.why_it_exists: The request should force the distinction between model-only knowledge and runtime retrieval.

implementation_details.title: Ask a question only the notes answer
implementation_details.action: This imports search.py, written by the step 'Wrap the retriever as a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Invoke with a question whose answer is not general knowledge.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from search import search_notes; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[search_notes]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What does the notes file say about the retry limit?'}]}); [print(m.type) for m in r['messages']]"
implementation_details.expected_result: The list includes a `tool` message carrying the search result.
implementation_details.caution: The retrieval must happen for a question the model cannot already answer. Testing with 'what is Python' proves nothing.

example.summary: A question only the notes can answer triggers retrieval.
example.input: 'What does the notes file say about the retry limit?'
example.output: human / ai(tool call) / tool(...) / ai(final answer)
example.note: A question the model already knows will not trigger the tool.

stages.title: Verify retrieval use
stages.local_goal: Confirm the answer uses relevant retrieved information.
stages.why_it_exists: A retrieval call alone does not prove useful RAG behavior.
stages.local_outcome: A grounded response for the practice case.

implementation_details.title: Check the answer is backed by a retrieved chunk
implementation_details.action: This imports search.py, written by the step 'Wrap the retriever as a tool'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Confirm a tool message exists and the final answer quotes something from it.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from search import search_notes; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[search_notes]); r = a.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What do the notes say about the retry limit?'}]}); tool = [m for m in r['messages'] if m.type == 'tool']; assert tool, 'nothing was retrieved'; print('grounded in', len(tool[0].content), 'chars')"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `grounded in N chars`.
implementation_details.caution: Asserting on the presence of a tool message is the check that matters. Comparing the answer to an expected string tests the model, not the agent.

example.summary: The final answer is backed by retrieved text.
example.note: Asserting on presence of retrieval, not on the answer's exact wording.

stages.title: Choose a control behavior
stages.local_goal: Select the execution behavior that needs control.
stages.why_it_exists: Middleware should solve a concrete harness concern such as retries, guardrails, transformation, summarization, or approval.

implementation_details.title: Name the behaviour that needs controlling
implementation_details.action: Write down the specific failure being prevented before choosing middleware.
implementation_details.command: python -c "open('control.md','w').write('Failure to prevent: the agent calls the delete_project tool on a request that mentions removing something.\nRequired behaviour: refuse unless the request contains the word CONFIRM.\n')"
implementation_details.expected_result: `cat control.md` prints one line beginning `Failure to prevent:` and one beginning `Required behaviour:`.
implementation_details.caution: Choosing middleware first and looking for a use case afterwards produces a guardrail that guards nothing.

example.summary: One failure and one required behaviour, written down.
example.output: refuse unless the request contains CONFIRM
example.note: Middleware chosen before the failure is a guardrail that guards nothing.

stages.title: Configure middleware
stages.local_goal: Create/configure the middleware behavior.
stages.why_it_exists: Middleware exposes hooks around agent execution and needs explicit behavior/configuration.

implementation_details.title: Write the guardrail middleware
implementation_details.action: Hook the model call and raise unless the text carries the confirmation word.
implementation_details.expected_result: `python -c "import guard"` exits 0, defining the class.
implementation_details.caution: Raising from a hook stops the run. Returning None lets it continue, so a guard that returns None unconditionally guards nothing.

example.summary: The guard raises on an unconfirmed request.
example.input: before_model checks the last message for 'CONFIRM'
example.note: Returning None continues the run; raising is what stops it.

stages.title: Attach middleware to the agent
stages.local_goal: Pass middleware into the agent harness.
stages.why_it_exists: The behavior must execute inside the agent's compiled runtime.

implementation_details.title: Pass the middleware into create_agent
implementation_details.action: This imports guard.py, written by the step 'Write the guardrail middleware'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Include the instance in the middleware list at construction.
implementation_details.command: python -c "from langchain.agents import create_agent; from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI; from guard import RequireConfirm; a = create_agent(ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), tools=[], middleware=[RequireConfirm()]); print('created')"
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `created`.
implementation_details.caution: Order matters: an outer middleware sees the request first. Putting a logging middleware outside the guard means it records the refused attempts too.

example.summary: The guarded agent is constructed.
example.note: An outer middleware sees the request first and the response last.

stages.title: Verify changed behavior
stages.local_goal: Run a case that triggers the middleware behavior.
stages.why_it_exists: The control is only useful if its effect is observable in execution.

implementation_details.title: Assert the guard blocks and then allows
implementation_details.action: This imports guard.py, written by the step 'Write the guardrail middleware'. The process order is what makes it exist; running this Stage on its own fails with ModuleNotFoundError, which means the step was skipped rather than that the code is wrong. Run one request without the word and one with it.
implementation_details.expected_result: The script prints `guard works`.
implementation_details.caution: Only testing the blocked case passes trivially. Also run an allowed request, or you have verified a middleware that refuses everything.

example.summary: The guard blocks one request and allows another.
example.note: Testing only the blocked case passes even for a middleware that refuses everything.

concepts.name: LangChain
concepts.definition: The framework providing the configurable create_agent harness and related agent components.
concepts.role: Supplies the high-level agent construction layer.

concepts.name: Agent
concepts.definition: A model operating in a loop that can use tools until the task is complete.
concepts.role: Coordinates task execution around the model loop.

concepts.name: Harness
concepts.definition: Everything around the model loop that supplies context and shapes behavior, including prompt, tools, and middleware.
concepts.role: Makes the raw model useful for a concrete agent application.

concepts.name: Model
concepts.definition: The language model selected for the agent.
concepts.role: Interprets messages, produces outputs, and chooses tool calls.

concepts.name: Message
concepts.definition: A structured conversational input or output passed through the agent state.
concepts.role: Carries user, model, and tool communication through execution.

concepts.name: Tool
concepts.definition: A callable external capability exposed to the agent.
concepts.role: Lets the agent fetch information or perform actions beyond model generation.

concepts.name: Tool schema
concepts.definition: The name, description, and argument contract through which a model understands how to call a tool.
concepts.role: Connects natural-language tool selection to valid callable input.

concepts.name: Tool result
concepts.definition: The output returned by a tool execution to the agent loop.
concepts.role: Feeds external information/action outcomes back to the model.

concepts.name: Agent loop
concepts.definition: The repeated model → optional tool execution → model cycle that continues until no more tools are needed.
concepts.role: Explains the runtime behavior of a tool-using agent.

concepts.name: State
concepts.definition: The information carried across agent execution, including conversation messages and other agent data.
concepts.role: Makes multi-step or multi-turn behavior possible.

concepts.name: Persistence
concepts.definition: The mechanism that stores and recovers agent state between executions.
concepts.role: Turns ephemeral state into continuing conversational state.

concepts.name: Thread
concepts.definition: A conversation/execution identity used to group related state across turns.
concepts.role: Provides the continuity boundary for a stateful interaction.

concepts.name: Knowledge source
concepts.definition: External documents, databases, APIs, or other information that can be queried at runtime.
concepts.role: Provides information that is not reliably contained in the model context or training.

concepts.name: Retrieval
concepts.definition: Fetching relevant external knowledge at query time.
concepts.role: Adds runtime context and supports RAG.

concepts.name: Prompt
concepts.definition: Instructions/context supplied to shape agent/model behavior.
concepts.role: Tells the agent how to approach the task and use available capabilities.

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.definition: Hooks and components that control or transform agent execution around the core loop.
concepts.role: Adds guardrails, retries, transformations, summarization, human approval, and other execution policies.

operations.name: Install
operations.definition: Make the required framework/provider package available.
common_failures: Installed into the system interpreter, so the project's venv cannot see the package.
A stale virtual environment from an earlier project shadows the new install.

operations.name: Configure
operations.definition: Supply the settings or behavior required for a component to operate.
operations.purpose: Prepare models, persistence, prompts, or middleware.
common_failures: The setting is supplied but never read, because the component was already constructed.
A value is set in one module and read in another that was never given it.

operations.name: Create
operations.definition: Construct a runtime object from configured components.
common_failures: A string is passed where a model instance is expected, producing a type error.
The component is created before its configuration is complete.

operations.name: Invoke
operations.definition: Execute a model or agent with an input message/state.
common_failures: A thread_id or config is missing on a stateful agent, and the error names invoke rather than the missing config.
The result is indexed as an object when it is a dict, so .content raises AttributeError.

operations.name: Inspect
operations.definition: Read execution output or state to understand what occurred.
operations.purpose: Connect runtime behavior to the mental model.
common_failures: messages[0] is read as the answer, but it is the message that was sent.
Output is printed in full, so the one line that matters is lost in the volume.

operations.name: Define
operations.definition: Describe and implement a callable capability or contract.
operations.purpose: Create tools and their callable schema.
common_failures: A tool has no docstring, so the model has nothing to match the request against.
The function's type hints do not describe the real input, so the generated schema lies.

operations.name: Attach
operations.definition: Connect an optional capability to the agent harness.
operations.purpose: Add tools, persistence, retrieval, or middleware.
common_failures: The tool or middleware is added to a list after the agent was constructed, so it is never bound.
Middleware is ordered inside-out, so the outer guard never sees the request first.

operations.name: Verify
operations.definition: Check that the intended operational behavior actually occurred.
operations.purpose: Validate the Goal rather than only configuration.
common_failures: Only the passing case is tested, so a component that refuses everything looks correct.
The assertion compares against model wording, which changes without any code change.

operations.name: Select
operations.definition: Choose an implementation or behavior appropriate to the local goal.
operations.purpose: Choose providers, middleware type, or architecture branch.
common_failures: A capability is chosen before the failure it should prevent is written down.
Two capabilities are added at once, so neither can be shown to work.

operations.name: Prepare
operations.definition: Make an external resource usable by a later Stage.
common_failures: The document path is wrong, producing zero chunks and a retrieval tool that never fires.
Chunks are too large to retrieve precisely, so every query returns most of the corpus.

operations.name: Retrieve
operations.definition: Fetch relevant external information for the current query.
operations.purpose: Supply runtime knowledge to the agent/model.
common_failures: The tool returns an empty string, so the model reads it as 'nothing found' rather than as a failure.
Retrieval is never triggered because the question is answerable from general knowledge.

operations.name: Persist
operations.definition: Store agent state for later recovery.
common_failures: An in-memory checkpointer is used in a process that restarts, and the history is lost.
A new thread_id is generated per request, so every call is a separate conversation.

branches.title: Choose model provider
branches.description: LangChain supports multiple model providers through a standard interface; provider choice changes configuration more than process structure.

branches.title: Choose tool representation
branches.description: A tool may be a Python callable, LangChain tool, or compatible tool description.

branches.title: Add structured output
branches.description: Extend agent output from free-form messages to schema-constrained structured data.

branches.title: Choose RAG architecture
branches.description: Use 2-step RAG, agentic RAG, or a hybrid pattern depending on control and flexibility needs.

branches.title: Choose middleware behavior
branches.description: Examples include logging, prompt/tool transformations, retries, fallbacks, guardrails, summarization, and human-in-the-loop approval.

branches.title: Move to advanced LangGraph orchestration
branches.description: When the topology is more than a standard agent loop, embed the agent inside a broader LangGraph workflow.

practices.title: Create and invoke a minimal agent
instructions: Install LangChain and one provider integration.
Configure a model.
Create an agent with a short system prompt.
Invoke it with one user message.
Inspect the final message.
practices.expected_outcome: A minimal LangChain agent returns a response.
checkpoint_questions: What is the difference between the Model and the Agent harness?
What object carries the user's input?

practices.title: Build a weather tool agent
instructions: Define a weather lookup tool.
Create an agent with the tool.
Ask a question that requires the tool.
Inspect execution and confirm the tool result feeds the final response.
practices.expected_outcome: The agent selects the weather tool and returns an answer based on its result.
checkpoint_questions: Why is defining a Tool different from calling it?
What loop occurs after the model chooses a Tool?

practices.title: Continue a two-turn conversation
instructions: Configure a persistence/checkpoint mechanism.
Create the agent with persistence.
Invoke a first message under a thread.
Invoke a second message under the same thread that depends on the first.
Verify the earlier context is available.
practices.expected_outcome: The second turn uses state from the first turn.
checkpoint_questions: What does persistence add that a normal invocation lacks?
Why does a thread identity matter?

practices.title: Build a documentation lookup agent
instructions: Prepare a small documentation source.
Expose a retrieval/fetch capability as a Tool.
Create an agent with instructions to use retrieval when needed.
Ask a source-dependent question.
Verify the answer uses retrieved content.
practices.expected_outcome: The agent retrieves external knowledge only when needed and uses it in the answer.
checkpoint_questions: How is agentic RAG different from always retrieving first?
Where does Retrieval connect to the Agent loop?

practices.title: Add one visible execution control
instructions: Choose one middleware behavior such as retry or human approval.
Configure the middleware.
Attach it to create_agent.
Run a case that triggers it.
Verify its effect.
practices.expected_outcome: The middleware visibly changes execution behavior.
checkpoint_questions: Why is Middleware part of the Harness rather than the Model?
When would a broader LangGraph workflow be more appropriate?
